newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU vets nuclear deal under other anti-trust rules.
newsitem.headline: EU vets nuclear deal under other anti-trust rules.

text.p: The European Commission will likely review a joint venture between Russian state-controlled AO Techsnabexport (Tenex) and RSB Logistic Projektspedition GmbH under EU rules which bans anti-competitive agreements.
The European Union executive earlier said the deal did not fall under the bloc's merger regulation which bans the creation or strengthening of a dominant position on the market.
The Commission said that according to its analysis the joint venture would not be a "full function one" and did not therefore fall under the scope of the merger regulation.

"It lacks the necessary assets such as special transportation equipment, specialised staff or know-how which would enable it to provide forwarding services for nuclear products on the market," it said in a statement.
Instead, it added, "the agreement now falls to be examined under other applicable competition rules."
An EU source said this meant it would probably be reviewed under article 85 of the EU's Treaty of Rome, which prohibits agreements which prevent, restrict or distort competition.
A key difference between the merger regulation and article 85 is that a review under the former has a time limit of one month. A probe under article 85 does not have a fixed deadline.
The deal was submitted to the Commission for clearance on February 26 under the EU's merger rules

Under the terms of the deal, RSB, which is ultimately controlled by German energy group RWE, and Tenex will take joint control of Fuel Logistic GmbH by way of purchase of shares in a newly created joint company.

Fuel Logistic provides services including transport for products used in the nuclear industry mainly in trade with Russia. Tenex exports metals, uranium-containing substances and other non-military nuclear products.
